html:
The baptism of Mieszko I, duke of the Polans, in 966, usually taken as the founding moment of the Polish state. Poland marked its millennium in 1966.

Mieszko ruled lands around Gniezno and Poznań. The year before, he had married Dobrawa, a Christian princess of Bohemia, and he took baptism from the Latin church rather than from Byzantium. That made him one of the Christian princes of Europe and took away a pretext the German lords of the Holy Roman Empire used for wars against pagan Slavs.

A bishopric followed at Poznań in 968. In 1000 the emperor Otto III came to Gniezno, where an archbishopric was founded, and Mieszko's son Bolesław the Brave was crowned the first king in 1025. Choosing Rome tied Poland to Western Europe and Latin letters, while its eastern neighbours took the Orthodox faith with the baptism of Rus' in 988. Poland later joined with Lithuania, the last pagan state in Europe, to form Poland and Lithuania.
